thread:
alex: Quick heads-up — ran an nsys trace on the TensorRT<->vLLM wrapper with the new KV-prefetch heuristic. Timeline shows a lot of tiny host->device memcpys interleaved with short kernel launches and a scheduler spin loop. attaching quick notes :eyes:

maria: can you paste the nsys summary / top timeline snippet?

alex: pasted minimal excerpt from the trace (cleaned):

```
nsys timeline: 0ms - 1.2s
NVTX: SCHED_DISPATCH [0.0 - 1.2s] many small spans (~800)
CUDA memcpy H2D: 0.2s total, ~750 calls (avg 260us)
Kernel launches (tiny kernels): 0.15s total, ~900 calls
ENGINE_INIT/LOAD: 0.08s total, ~120 calls (120us each)
CPU spin (scheduler loop): ~0.42s (35% wall)
Wrapper overhead (vLLM call + context switch NVTX): ~0.34s (28%)
Other GPU compute: 0.25s
```

alex: tl;dr: lots of small memcpys + engine init churn. scheduler spin dominates wall time.

cheng: that ENGINE_INIT count stands out — are we recreating engine or doing per-request fallback? iirc the fallback path can call `tensorrt::Engine::load` when kernel select fails.

sam: Confirmed on the trace: the NVTX name for the failing kernel is "kernel_select_fallback" and it's invoked from the wrapper hotpath when sequence lengths hit a certain threshold. Fallback path is not debounced. :bug: 

maria: any chance prefetch is sequential in the scheduler? I remember a change that moved prefetch into the dispatch loop. Sequential H2D would explain the ~750 memcpy calls.

alex: yes — current prefetch code issues one memcpy per token group inside the scheduler loop. That shows up as many small H2D ops.

sam: repro command I used (so you can replicate):

```
docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/work -w /work rwinf/profiler:latest \ 
  nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=/tmp/trace \ 
  ./benchmark_infer --model rtd-8b --seq 1024 --batch 1 --warm 10 --iters 50
```

alex: also attached the quick perf stat from the profiler summary: scheduler spin 34%, wrapper overhead 28%, memcpy H2D 18%, kernels 12%, idle 8%.

julie: interesting — if engine init is 120us and it happens ~120 times per trace that's ~14ms just for engine churn. combined with the spin it's significant.

cheng: proposed small experiment list: 1) add NVTX around engine init to confirm attribution, 2) debounce fallback so it only triggers once per sequence-length bucket, 3) coalesce prefetch memcpys into a single async H2D for all KV pages, 4) try CUDA graph capture for the warm path.

maria: agree. also try running CUDA occupancy / kernel selection offline to avoid fallback at runtime (precompute kernel choice for common lengths).

alex: I already ran a quick patched trace where we coalesced memcpys (local branch). Results: memcpy calls dropped from ~750 -> ~6, H2D time went from 0.2s -> 0.03s, overall p50 latency improved ~9%. Still seeing wrapper + spin => next target.

sam: solid. can you push the branch? I can run full perf suite. :thumbsup: 

julie: i'll open a PR to debounce the kernel fallback and add an NVTX flag to the engine init path. assigning to @cheng + @sam for measurement.

ci-bot: perf-regression-monitor: detected 7.8% p50 regression on commit bf3a2e3 vs baseline; likely area: scheduler/dispatch.

alex: thanks. plan: merge coalesce memcpys first (low-risk), then debounce fallback + NVTX. after each PR we run the nsys job with the same reproducible script and compare timeline.

maria: one more idea — if we can precompute kernel selection table per model/seq-range at startup (cheap), we avoid runtime select entirely for 90% of requests. small memory tradeoff.

cheng: i'll prototype the precompute table and NVTX-annotate everything so perf diffs are clearer.

sam: note for the run: use `nsys stats -a /tmp/trace.qdrep` to get kernel count and `nsys profile --export=sqlite` then `nsys-ui` to inspect memcopy stacks.

alex: awesome. thanks everyone. i'll post the before/after traces in this thread once the PR is merged. :hammer: 

julie: assigning the checklist in the PR: coalesce-prefetch (julie), debounce-fallback (cheng), nvtx-engine-init (maria), perf-runbook update (sam).

alex: cool — tagging @eng-sre to run the long-run bench after these land.

maria: any timeline?

julie: aiming for EOD tomorrow for coalesce PR, rest by midweek.

alex: perfect. closing the loop here, we'll re-run same docker nsys command and attach traces.
